newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Mobutu, Moi to meet on eastern Zaire crisis.
newsitem.headline: Mobutu, Moi to meet on eastern Zaire crisis.

text.p: Kenyan President Daniel arap Moi flies to Zaire on Monday for a meeting with President Mobutu Sese Seko to discuss the continuing crisis in the Great Lakes region, Kenyan Foreign Minister Stephen Musyoka said on Sunday.

Musyoka said the meeting at Mobutu's jungle palace of Gbadolite was a follow-up to last December's Nairobi summit of 10 African leaders, boycotted by Kinshasa, which discussed the deteriorating situation in central Africa after ethnic Tutsi rebels seized control of eastern Zaire.
"My president's mission will be aimed at communicating the decisions of the Nairobi summit to President Mobutu," Musyoka told Reuters.
Musyoka, who was in Harare for a Zimbabwe-Kenya joint commission meeting to look at ways of promoting trade between the two countries, said Monday's meeting was at Mobutu's invitation.
He said Mobutu had also invited South Africa's Nelson Mandela, Zimbabwe's Robert Mugabe and Cameroonian President and Organisation of African Unity chairman Paul Biya to Gbadolite.
But Zimbabwean officials said Mugabe could not make it due to a prior commitment and Musyoka said it was unclear whether Biya and Mandela would attend.

He denied suggestions that the meeting was aimed at patching up strained relations between Nairobi and Kinshasa following accusations by Zaire that the December summit was organised by English-speaking African countries to destabilise it.
"There's no tension at all between us. Those remarks by the (Zairean) information minister were due to misunderstanding of the Nairobi summit," Musyoka said.
He said Moi, Mandela, Mugabe and Biya were tasked by the Nairobi summit to secure an early meeting with Mobutu to discuss ways of resolving the central African crisis.
"The intention of my president is to brief his colleagues as soon as he comes back from Gbadolite," Musyoka said.

On what Kenya expected to come out of Monday's meeting, he said: "In Africa, when a neighbour's house is on fire you do what you can to assist to put it out. But the issues in Zaire are intricate...We have to continue to respect Zaire's territorial integrity. That is very important.

"President Moi will not be expected to go to Zaire and lecture them on their internal situation. It must be the Zairoises who must take leadership in resolving their problems. This is an internal matter and they must help us to resolve the situation which has spilt over into the region," he said.
